adjudications.flag: request_reference_hash=false for baseline, cartesian, and two_link_ik
adjudications.finding: The checker compared request.replay_motion to the NPZ file-byte SHA-256. The request contract deliberately uses the canonical NPZ-content hash implemented by motion_hash(), including sorted key, dtype, shape, and array bytes. Recomputed content hashes equal all three requests. This removes the alleged current-artifact mismatch, but it does not close the separate execution-time TOCTOU gap: the child collector did not recompute replay_motion after loading the replay file.

The checker hard-coded replay as the source-construction mode. The fixed V51 source construction is natively generated val/seed11/round0 evidence. Its actual request, lineage, seed, scope, case order, source hashes, and 24-by-3 construction all match. No result is reclassified by this adjudication.

The script required bitwise equality. The effective lineage contract accepts the upstream float32 root subtract/re-add canonical transform at absolute tolerance 1e-12. Across all three arms, raw-to-canonical maximum error is 1.866893570624082e-16 m, while selected-to-canonical and raw-to-selected differences are float32 roundoff at 5.960464477539063e-08 m. The documented invariant passes.

Trace positions, previous-position recurrence, frame indices, and zero first velocity are exact. A NumPy re-evaluation of the float32 subtraction/division differs by at most 9.5367431640625e-07 m/s for the three arms; the retained same-arithmetic CUDA audit matches all 622080 scalars exactly. No contract requires cross-runtime bitwise equality, and no gate/classification depends on the stricter assertion.
